title: Social protection that scales up in heatwaves
disclaimer: Listing is not endorsement and is not financial, insurance or investment advice.
scope_note: Source-checked scoping review, not an exhaustive systematic review. Heterogeneous scheme records must not be counted as heat-triggered cash programmes. Sources accessible in this review include documents with subsequent intermittent failures; access limitations recorded. No heat-specific paid aggregate inferred from entitlement, budget or announcement.
schema_notes: The six supplied top-level arrays are retained. Additional metadata, legal/benefit fields, money ledger and unverified list make scope and missing evidence explicit.
'not verified' is missing evidence, not zero. Empty payouts means no admitted transaction, not no payment.
Scheme level identifies financing/administration; instruments can serve another level. Public social insurance is mapped to social rather than equated with a private parametric transfer.
Source.label uses the required evidence labels; access quality is separately recorded in source_register.
Sources on benefit rules are guidance, not causal evidence. Loop and lever mappings are analytical inferences.
No published head-to-head heat comparison found in the reviewed evidence.

instruments.name: Public employment with heat-safe working arrangements
instruments.plain_definition: Government offers eligible people paid work; heat rules can change work conditions. A worksite rule does not itself create a heat cash entitlement.
instruments.how_it_breaks_the_cycle: Potential mechanism: pre-arranged finance can reduce uncompensated income or care costs and avoid emergency reallocations. These loop links are analytical mappings, not measured causal effects.
instruments.risk_holder: Underlying household/worker heat risk; public authority, employer or fund holds the specified financial obligation.
instruments.speed: Payment follows work/muster/payroll rules, not automatically a weather warning.
instruments.typical_cost: No transferable heat-specific unit-cost estimate verified. Distinguish benefit spending, administration, contributions/premiums and cost of capital; none can be inferred from an entitlement limit.
instruments.strengths: Can use established eligibility, service or payment infrastructure; verified example below establishes design, not universal effective coverage.
instruments.limits: Task and attendance rules can conflict with protective rest; full-wage shorter days require explicit authorization.
instruments.basis_risk: Usually eligibility, exposure and delivery mismatch rather than weather-index basis risk; do not label every exclusion as actuarial basis risk.
instruments.reaches_poorest_why: Depends on programme coverage, documentation, connection/registration and accessible last-mile delivery. Existing infrastructure does not establish universal reach.
